subject: Misrouted to me: Fabio's B3 verdict (bottom-right = 144/512, the CLIPPING run) + the wavy-shadow artifact is MPI-506 defect 3, color_correction_method
body:
WHAT HAPPENED

Fabio pasted the B3 grid video (B3_grid_h264) into the WRONG session. It landed in
mine - the MPI-536 LTX 2.3 foley Flow session - and he caught it a couple of turns
later and asked me to forward it to you. So the B3 verdict you have been waiting on
exists; it just went to the wrong agent.

WHAT I DID, so you can trust the state of the tree

- Read only: tasks/MPI-506/brief.md (sections 2d-2e) and tasks/MPI-557/brief.md +
  plan.md, to identify the artifact he described.
- Edited NOTHING of yours. No card, no column, no plan, no brief, no workflow. Your
  uncommitted MPI-557 changes in the working tree are untouched.
- Ran no generations and queued nothing. I checked that the bench on 8188 answers
  (it does, HTTP 200) and stopped there - I did not read its history or touch it.
- Your card stays in `doing`. I did not move it.
- For completeness on shared state: my own session added MPI-536 to `doing` and
  committed 64d7de66 (a raw workflow source under comfy_workflows/raw/). Nothing in
  that path is yours.

FABIO'S B3 VERDICT - verbatim: "the bottom right one is the best one"

That is the `512 pad1.33 CLIPS` tile: window 144, sample 512, 385 face px, 34.4 s,
12.58 GiB.

It is also the run your own table flags as CLIPPING the travel envelope - 7 px off
the top, 8 px off the bottom. So his eye picked the tightest framing, which is
simultaneously the fastest, the cheapest in VRAM, the highest in delivered face
pixels, AND the one that cuts the chin.

That tension is yours to resolve, and it is a real fork, not a detail: either the
travel-union rule wants a smaller pad than 1.63, or he judged the grid on frames
where the clip does not actually cut. Before treating 144 as the answer, show him
the specific frames where the chin leaves the window - your own measurement says
the face travels through a 115 x 160 px envelope while measuring 108 px tall, so
the clipping is real and locatable.

THE ARTIFACT HE FLAGGED, ACROSS EVERY TILE - already solved once on this codebase

Fabio: "these are all suffering a little bit from what we had going on when we set
up SeedVR2 for the first time, which is wavy kind of shadows on the video ... in
still frames you can't really see it, but when you look at the video you can. Like
clouds moving on top of the video."

That is MPI-506 section 2e, DEFECT 3: `color_correction_method` on
`SeedVR2PostProcessing`. The measured table from that card (drift p2..p98 / max abs
drift / sharpness):

  none     -3.00..+14.00 /  36 / 5.79   <- what the official templates ship
  lab      -1.00..+8.00  /  19 / 5.31   <- the SHIPPED value, and the node default
  wavelet  -1.00..+9.00  /  20 / 5.40
  adain    -7.00..+7.00  /  43 / 5.08

His words at the time were "shadowy blobs on her face and body". It was proven NOT
to be tile seams: a seam-gradient test on the 512/128 VAE tile grid returned ratio
1.02, i.e. no grid structure. It is smooth low-frequency LUMA DRIFT - invisible in
a still, reads as clouds sliding over the picture in motion. That is exactly the
symptom he is describing now.

THE GAP IN YOUR SWEEP: your arms compared `none` (arm B) and `wavelet` (arm C),
found them indistinguishable, and concluded colour correction had little to correct
on this clip. `lab` - the value the app actually ships - was never in that
comparison. If the B3 runs used `none`, the drift is simply uncorrected, and the
"B and C are the same" result is consistent with that rather than evidence against
it (none 36 vs wavelet 20 differ on drift but barely on the laplacian you scored).

CHEAP TO SETTLE: correction is a post-process, so the sampler output stays
`execution_cached` and each variant costs ~10-20 s. Re-run one B3 config with
`color_correction_method: lab` and put it next to the same config with `none`.

ALREADY RULED OUT for B3, from your own notes - do not spend runs here:

- Chunking / seams: `auto` logged `frames_per_chunk=73` over 73 frames, so the whole
  clip was ONE chunk. There is no join to see.
- DEFECT 1 (`temporal_overlap = 8` clamps to step 1, Hann-merging ~3 independently
  sampled restorations into ghosting) needs at least two chunks to bite. Single
  chunk means it cannot be the cause here.

Source for all of the above: tasks/MPI-506/brief.md sections 2d-2e.

recent_events.note: Verdict received: bottom-right = 144/512 CLIPS tile. Acting on both halves - colour-correction gap (runs used none, app ships lab) and the clipping fork.
